text:
alana (product): Quick sync — for the Q3 cutover we need a concise checklist for staged cutover criteria + rollback ladder. Can we agree on concrete gate metrics so on-call and PMs know exactly when to abort?

matt (eng): +1. I sketched something: region by region ramps (0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%), canary duration 30m for initial small slice, then 2h for the broader ramp. Abort if any hard SLO breaches.

jordan (sre): Can we enumerate the SLOs and thresholds? My proposal: 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m OR p95 latency > 1.2s increase vs baseline by >25% -> automatic pause and alert.

tara (cs): From customers' perspective, we also need a clear customer-impact checklist: "if top-10 customers show errors or >2x latency" then trigger hold and manual rollback.

matt (eng): Agree. Also want a safe fallback variant: flag routes traffic to model-v1-fallback (smaller model) when threshold hit, not full revert to infra. That buys us time.

jordan (sre): SRE automation idea: use a 3-step rollback ladder
- step 1: throttle to 10% and switch to fallback-variant
- step 2: if still bad after 15m, route entire slice back to previous stable model (model-v1)
- step 3: full feature-flag kill and global rollback if step2 fails

matt (eng): I'll add those as explicit actions in the flag playbook. Snippet for rollout policy (to put in console):
```yaml
flag: new_routing_cutover
steps:
  - pct: 0.5
    duration: 30m
    checks: ["5xx < 0.5%", "p95_delta < 25%"]
  - pct: 5
    duration: 2h
  - pct: 20
    duration: 2h
  - pct: 100
    duration: 1h
fallback_variant: model-v1-fallback
rollback_ladder: [throttle->fallback, revert-model, kill-flag]
```

alana (product): Love that. Can we also codify observability and owner handoffs? For each step assign an owner: engineer oncall, product lead, and CS rep. And a timeline: if step1 is triggered, SRE takes first action within 5m.

jordan (sre): Yep. I'll add runbook entries: owner tags and automated Slack pings. Example alert copy: `ALERT: new_routing_cutover — p95 spike in eu-west (2.0s) — action: throttle to 10% and switch to fallback`.

tara (cs): Also request: add a customer holdback knob for enterprise customers (per-tenant opt-out). We need a simple toggle that keeps specific tenants on old path.

matt (eng): There is already per-tenant flagging support. Will add a guard to default those VIP tenants to previous route during the first 2 ramps.

jordan (sre): We should define the A/B evaluation window and metrics to decide rollout success beyond infra health: quality regressions (BLEU/QA accuracy delta), customer-support tickets, and manual CS thumbs. Proposed pass criteria after 100%: no quality regression > 2% on core evals, < 0.3% increase in overall 5xx, and no >3 high-severity customer incidents within 24h.

alana (product): That covers it. Next steps: Matt to put flag config + playbook into the Console docs, Jordan to update runbook and automation, Tara to prep a customer comms snippet and VIP opt-out list. I'll schedule a 15m pre-cutover dry run with oncall and CS.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled — new_routing_cutover staged rollout starting 2024-07-18T16:00Z (canary slice).

matt (eng): I'll post the final playbook link here once done. tagging @jordan @tara for visibility :raised_hands:

jordan (sre): quick Q: should we enable automatic rollback or just automated pause and notify? I prefer pause + scripted rollback to avoid accidental global kill.

alana (product): Pause + scripted rollback sounds safer. We'll make automatic rollback an option but default to manual confirmation after step2.

matt (eng): noted. I'll default auto_rollback: false in the config.

tara (cs): thanks — i'll assemble the VIP list and send it to matt by EOD. :shipit:

alana (product): Great work team — we'll iterate but this gives ops the clear ladder they asked for.
